characters.name: Gus
characters.description: A deer hybrid raised in the wilderness and the main protagonist, Gus is a good hearted, cheerful and naive young boy who has little knowledge of the world around him as a result of his sheltered lifestyle. Artificial Human:Inepisode 7, he is revealed to have been created in a lab and is very likely the first-ever hybrid child. Brats with Slingshots:Deconstructed. Gus has excellent aim with his slingshot and attempts to use it to defend himself on several occasions. However, at just ten years old, he doesn't have the strength to make the strikes actually hurt his opponents. Dark and Troubled Past: He knows nothing about his past, only that his "Pubba" (aka Dad) took him far away into the forest and barricaded them from the rest of the world, which his dad told him was dangerous. For a decade, he only knew his sheltered life.His dad later dies after they're spotted and he leaves the campsite to kill the man to keep Gus safe and comes back Sick. After this, Gus is left on his own for a year before leaving to find his mother, whom he was told couldn't be with him and still out there. In the season 1 finale, he learns the truth of his past: he was created in a lab by scientists as the very first of the hybrid children. He was on the verge of being taken by the government to be experimented on, but scientist Birdie (his "mother") grew to love him and wasdesperate to protect him. Along with Richard assisting (his "dad" who was the building's janitor), she broke Gus out of the lab and convinced Richard to adopt Gus as she stayed behind to destroy her research (which she warned could kill millions). This was how Richard and Gus ended up in the forest and how Birdie was separated from them. Cheerful Child: He seems to be a happy kid overall, although he does sometimes have issues like nightmares as a result of everything he's endured.

characters.name: Jepperd
characters.description: A lone drifter with a troubled past. He reluctantly accompanies Gus on his journey, who gives him the nickname of "Big Man". Adaptational Heroism: Downplayed in the show. While he's still rough around the edges and his backstory is kept intact, the show did tweak his character. One major change was, in the comic, Jepperd betrays Gus to the Last Men with the promise of seeing his wife again,which would later turn out he specifically wanted to be given his dead wife's body. In the show, he doesn't betray Gus to the Last Men; he gets shot by them instead, allowing them to take Gus as Jepperd is too wounded to intervene. He also warms up to Gus and becomes a father figure to him far quicker compared to the comic. Adaptational Job Change: His former occupation was a hockey player in the comic series, in this adaption he is an ex-football player. The Big Guy: Gus's nickname for him is "Big Man" because of his large size. Dark and Troubled Past: He initially had a good life, but when his wife gave birth to their child during the Great Crumble, he discovered his baby was a hybrid andwas distraught. By the time he gathered the courage to love his new family and went to be by their side, he found the government had already taken them away. Now alone and struggling to survive the harsh new world, he became a Last Man and poached hybrid children to get by, tearing families apart in the hope of earning the connections that could find his wife and son. Afterfinding that they had already been murdered by the Last Men], he left the organization and simply decided to survive on his own. While admitting he isn't proud of what he did, he firmly sticks to his past actions as being "what he needed to do to survive". However, it's implied that what he did still haunts him and his choice to help Gusis an attempt to ease his guilt(as well as a hope to rebuild his life again).

characters.name: Bear
characters.description: The former leader of the Animal Army, a group of teenagers dedicated to protecting the hybrid kids. However, after meeting Gus, she grew disillusioned by their extreme methods, and decided to leave to accompany Gus in his journey and protect him. Action Girl: She first appeared along with Tiger saving Gus and Jepperd by attacking the Last Men with her daggers. It's also shown that, as part of the Animal Army training, she and her fellow members must regularly train for combat and battle. Adult Hater: She claims to despise adults, due to the Last Men taking away her sister anddestroyed her life. She nearly attempts to kill Jepperd (due to him being a former member of the Last Men) until Gus convinces her not to do so. Even then, she did not get along with Jepperd at all early on until Gus called them out on their constant bickering. Adaptational Heroism: As the (former) leader of the Animal Army, she is much more goodhearted and far lessAx-Crazythan her comic book counterpart, Glebhelm. Animal Motifs: Chooses the Bear as her animal representation in the Animal Army she created.

characters.name: Wendy
characters.description: A pig hybrid girl who befriends Gus when they're both captured by Abbott. She later becomes one of his companions after they escape. Doorstop Baby: She was found by Aimee at the entrance of The Preserve as a baby in a basket, presumably left there by her biological parents. In-Series Nickname: She's sometimes referred to as “Pigtails”. Long-Lost Relative: She’s the long lost little sister ofBear, though she isn’t aware of this at first, as she was just a baby when she was separated from her biological family as a baby. Their relationship is a little awkward at first whenBearreveals they are siblings, but by the end of the series they’ve developed a strong bond. The Nose Knows: Wendy has a quite potent sense of smell, being able to determine the number of Last Men outside of The Preserve through her nose.

characters.name: Dr. Adi Singh
characters.description: A doctor who is desperately looking for a cure for “the sick”, so he can save his wife, Rani, who’s infected by it. While a good person at heart, there is no length Adi won’t go if it means saving his wife. Affably Evil: He's a genuinely good-natured guy, quite courteous with Gus, and even acknowledges the fact that hybrids are intelligent beings, but that doesn't change the fact that he's willing to kill children and ally with some truly monstrous people if it means saving the people he loves... and later,saving the world by using Gus as aHuman Sacrifice. Beard of Sorrow: By season 3, he's grown a massive beard, having given up on grooming afterRani's departure and the failure of his cure.More worryingly, combined with his glasses, it makes Adi look worryingly like Abbottand isan early hintthat he's begun following his former boss into delusional extremism. Driven to Suicide: In the finale of season 2,after all his attempts at a cure fails and Rani leaves him in disgust over his refusal to give up on a futile quest, Adi retreats to a roomful of purple flowers so he can fatally poison himself. However, the final battle between the Last Men and Animal Army ends up breaking the observation window, allowing in enough oxygen so he can eventually regain consciousness - albeit with a few personality-shaping visions of the future crowding his brain. Exhausted Eye Bags: He gets those after he begins working with The Last Men, as he’s barely sleeping and spending every waking hour working to find a cure.

characters.name: Rani Singh
characters.description: Ascended Extra: In the comics, she died to “the Sick” in a flashback before the story begins. In the show, she survives the outbreak of the infection thanks to Adi and is one of the main characters. Like Brother and Sister:Downplayed. Rani forms a friendship with Johnny during her time as a hostage to the Last Men. He tries to make her feel comfortable at the Preserve and doesn’t treat her as just a way to force Dr. Adi to work for the Last Men. Rani in return stands up to Abbott for him and encourages Johnny to leave his abusive brother. There’s never any romantic feeling between them, as Rani is already married to Adi. Love Cannot Overcome:By the end of season two, Rani is tired from all the things she and Adi do to keep her alive. From working with bad people like Abbott, to all the stress Abi is putting himself through, tokillingthe animal children to make a cure, it’s too much for her. She asks her husband to just run away with her and enjoy the short time they still have together. But when it becomes clear that Adi is too obsessed at this point to give up on the research, she leaves without him. Your Days Are Numbered: Rani is infected with “the Sick”, a virus with no known cure who is wiping out humanity. While her husband manages to make booster shots to halt the virus, it’s only a temporary solution and Rani is still going to die without a permanent cure.

characters.name: Jimmy Jacobs
characters.description: Sports Star to Scoundrel: In "Stranger Danger On A Train," Gus, Bear, and Jepperd run into Jimmy, another former football star and an old friend of Jepperd. Out of work in the wake of the Sick, Jimmy is also working for the Last Men as muscle, though as a simple grunt rather than a legendary hunter; it soon becomes clear that this is because Jimmy suffered alotof brain trauma over the course of his football career, leaving himextremely dim-wittedandforgetfulas a result.Thankfully, he sides with his friends over his employers,holding off the Last Menlong enough for Gus and co to escape the train.

characters.name: Richard Fox
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: Pubba is a loving father who sheltered Gus out of fear of the outside world harming him, (not unjustified given the Last Men and general bigoted people). Whereas in the comic, he is areligious fanaticdoing it because of delusions that Gus is a God. Anger Born of Worry: When Gus steps beyond the fence in the first episode out of simple curiosity, his father drags him back inside and yells at him. Nothing bad happened and Gus never actually left as he got scared and turned back. However, his father is shown to beProperly Paranoidas brutal hybrid poachers exist just outside the fence and most of the world wants to see hybrid children dead and view them as subhuman. Dead Person Conversation: He appears to Gus a few times after his death. First when Gus falls into the purple flowers in the Valley of Sorrows. Later, Gus hears his voice during Aditya's experiment on him to discover his origins. Finally, in the show's finale, he appears one final time to Gus in a vision to help him decide wethersave or condemn humanity. Good Parents: He was a loving parent to Gus and went to great lengths to protect him, from building their house in an isolated forest to being willing to face the Last Men to protect him. Even though he isn't his biological son, it's clear he loves him a lot. Promotion to Parent: He was entrusted with Gus by Birdie shortly after his first date with her. While he wasn’t very enthusiastic about it at first, he understood the importance of keeping the baby hybrid safe and grew to love him as his own son over the years.

characters.name: Abbott
characters.description: Bald of Evil: He's a bald, merciless and cruel man who has no problem in killing others as long as it gets him what he wants. Beard of Evil: In contrast with his clean head, he has a big, bushy beard. Big Brother Bully: Towards his younger brother, Johnny. He's verbally abusive and constantly diminishes him. Combat Pragmatist: Abbott does not believe in fighting fair, especially when he's pitted against a much bigger opponent. When the final battle pits him against Jepperd, Abbot wins by dealing a kick to Jepp's bad knee. Faux Affably Evil: He can come across as friendly and polite, but as it is quickly revealed, he is a ruthless, merciless and cruel monster who would do what it takes to get what he desires, even if that means killing others.

characters.name: Johnny
characters.description: General Abbott's younger brother who works as an assistant for him. He's very loyal to his brother, but doesn't have his ruthless disposition. Cain and Abel: The Abel to General Abbott's Cain. He's the younger, kinder sibling who doesn't really agree with the Last Men's methods, while The General is the older, ruthless one.He gets killed by his brother at the end of season 2 when he finally stands up against him. Pet the Dog: He goes out of his way to accommodate Rani despite her being a hostage to force Dr. Adi to cooperate with the Last Men. This gets him reprimanded by General Abbott, but he's still nice to Rani after it. Token Good Teammate: He's the nicest of the Last Men, even if that isn't a high bar to clear. He isn't cruel to the hybrid kids and tries to make Rani feel comfortable in the Preserve. The only reason he is a part of the Last Men is because his brother is the only family he has left. Noble Top Enforcer: He's the one General Abbott leaves in charge of the Preserve when he's not around. He's also not cruel like his brother or the other Last Men.
